description: We are Team ARTEGIX—driven by a shared passion for space exploration and Earth science. At the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we leverage cutting-edge satellite data, atmospheric insights, and space technology to revolutionize agriculture and smart farming. By bridging the gap between orbits and agriculture, our goal is to build sustainable, data-driven solutions to optimize crop yields, monitor environmental changes, and secure a resilient future for Earth.
summary:
TerraShift is an end-to-end agronomy decision-support platform that translates NASA Earth observation data into actionable, multi-season crop rotation strategies for farmers.

To address the challenge of agricultural decision-making under climate volatility, farmers simply draw their field boundary on an interactive map. TerraShift fuses 36-month NASA POWER agroclimatology and NASA AppEEARS satellite time series (MODIS/HLS NDVI, SMAP L4 root-zone soil moisture, and ECOSTRESS evaporative stress) with ISRIC SoilGrids, Copernicus DEM terrain slope, ECMWF SEAS5 seasonal forecasts, and FAOSTAT regional market economics. Its two-layer in-memory agronomy engine runs spatial-temporal Ridge regression to project 18-month water and climate anomalies, followed by a vectorized PyGAD Genetic Algorithm that evolves optimal 3-season crop rotations in under 15 milliseconds—paired with Google Gemini natural-language explanations and an interactive rotation planner.

By turning complex satellite telemetry into localized soil-resilient and market-optimized plans, TerraShift empowers farmers to prevent crop failure, conserve water, regenerate soil nitrogen, and protect their livelihoods against climate shocks.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

TerraShift is a geospatial agronomy decision-support platform that translates complex satellite Earth-observation data into actionable, multi-season crop rotation plans for farmers adapting to climate volatility and market shifts.

  1. Interactive Farm Mapping: Farmers map their field boundaries on an interactive Leaflet/Geoman map (2dsphere GeoJSON polygons validated with Turf.js for area and self-intersection) and specify their soil profile, irrigation availability, historical crops, and primary goal (Water Conservation, Soil Restoration, Profit Optimization, or Balanced).
  2. Step 0 — Spatial-Temporal Satellite Data Fusion (nasa_fusion.py): Given a farm’s centroid coordinates, TerraShift fetches 36 months of agroclimatology data from the NASA POWER API (T2M_MAX, PRECTOTCORR, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, EVPTRNS), cached at a 0.01° spatial grid in Redis for 24 hours, and harmonizes it with NASA SMAP L4 root-zone soil moisture and MODIS/Sentinel-2 NDVI vegetation indices into a contiguous 36 × 6 NumPy tensor.
    • Plan A (A_BASELINE): Continuation of current monoculture practice.
    • Plan B (B_SOIL_WATER_RESILIENCE): Maximum drought resilience, nitrogen fixation, and soil cover.
    • Plan C (C_COST_MARKET_OPTIMIZED): Highest net profit and anti-oversupply market diversification.
  3. AI Agronomist Explainability (llmExplainer.ts): Google Gemini 2.5 Flash translates the quantitative projections and satellite trends into plain-language agronomic recommendations and step-by-step transition checklists.

What benefits does it have & what is the intended impact?

  • Bridging the "Last Mile" of Satellite Data: Farmers rarely have the tools to interpret raw netCDF/HDF5 satellite feeds. TerraShift converts NASA climate telemetry directly into seasonal crop choices, water savings (mm), nitrogen balance (kg/ha), and net profit ($/ha).
  • Preventing Monoculture Collapse & Regional Oversupply: When climate shifts occur, neighboring farms often switch to the same cash crop simultaneously, crashing local market prices. TerraShift accounts for regional crop saturation to protect farmer incomes.
  • Climate Resilience for Vulnerable Dry Zones: Tested against real-world regimes like Sri Lanka’s Dry Zone (Anuradhapura Maha/Yala cycles) and the US Midwest, TerraShift empowers smallholder and commercial farms to survive worsening droughts, reduce synthetic fertilizer reliance through strategic legume rotations, and regenerate degraded topsoil.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages: Python 3.12, TypeScript 5.7, JavaScript, Bash.
  • Earth Observation & Reference Data: NASA POWER Agroclimatology API, NASA SMAP Root-Zone Soil Moisture, MODIS/Sentinel-2 NDVI, FAO GAEZ (Global Agro-Ecological Zones), and USDA AMS Market News.
  • Agronomy Engine (agronomy-engine): FastAPI, Uvicorn, NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-Learn (Ridge), Pydantic v2, PyMongo.
  • Main API Service (main-service): Node.js 20, Express.js, Mongoose, Redis (ioredis), Google GenAI SDK (@google/genai with gemini-2.5-flash), Zod, JWT & bcryptjs, Helmet.
  • Frontend (frontend): Next.js 15 (App Router), React 19, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, React-Leaflet, Leaflet-Geoman, Turf.js (@turf/area, @turf/kinks), Recharts, Lucide Icons.
  • Databases & Infrastructure: MongoDB Atlas (Dual-Database architecture: lookup_db + general_db with 2dsphere geospatial indexes), Redis 7 (24-hour spatial grid cache), Docker & Docker Compose, Nginx reverse proxy, Let's Encrypt (Certbot + sslip.io), Ubuntu VPS, and Vercel with GitHub Actions CI/CD.

How is your project creative?

  1. Zero-I/O In-Memory Matrix Genetic Algorithm: Traditional decision-support tools query databases inside optimization loops, causing multi-second bottlenecks. TerraShift pre-fetches agronomic lookup tables (lookup_db) at startup into a contiguous 12 × 6 float64 NumPy matrix (memory_store.py), allowing the 30-generation Genetic Algorithm to evaluate 1,500 multi-season crop rotation scenarios in under 15 milliseconds with zero disk or network I/O.
  2. Spatial-Temporal + Market Co-Optimization: Rather than optimizing strictly for weather or strictly for yield, TerraShift couples physical satellite telemetry (soil moisture anomalies, evapotranspiration, NDVI degradation) with game-theoretic regional market saturation penalties—preventing localized price crashes.
  3. Side-by-Side Scenario Storytelling + Generative AI: Instead of prescribing a single black-box answer, TerraShift presents three transparent 3-season trajectories (Baseline vs. Soil/Water Resilience vs. Market-Optimized) paired with Gemini-generated narratives that cite specific NASA indicators.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Low-Resource & Rural Connectivity Constraints: We designed the backend to run on low-RAM cloud hosts without requiring a heavy local database instance by pairing MongoDB Atlas with a lightweight Redis spatial cache (nasa:grid:{lat}:{lon}) and in-memory NumPy arrays.
  • Graceful Degradation & Offline Fault Tolerance: Live satellite APIs, cloud databases, or LLM services can experience downtime or rate limits. We engineered deterministic fallbacks at every layer: nasa_fusion.py falls back to synthetic agro-climatic series if NASA POWER is unreachable, memory_store.py includes a local seed fallback if Atlas is offline, and llmExplainer.ts deterministically generates data-driven agronomic guidance if the Gemini API key is absent or rate-limited.
  • Agronomic Realism: Our 12-crop catalog (paddy_rice, mung_bean, cowpea, maize, finger_millet, groundnut, sesame, chilli, onion, sunn_hemp, chickpea, cassava) is grounded in FAO GAEZ water/nitrogen parameters and enforces real-world agronomy rules—such as penalizing consecutive high-water monocultures and rewarding nitrogen-fixing legume transitions.
